title: Causes of World War I
summary: World War I started mainly because of conflicts between countries in Europe. One major cause was the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in 1914, which led to a crisis and alliances forming between powerful countries like Germany, Austria-Hungary, France, Russia, and Britain. These countries were also competing for power through military build-up and imperialism, which made the situation tense and eventually led to the war.

title: World War I | Causes & Effects | Britannica
summary: World War I began after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria-Hungary in 1914, which increased tensions between countries. European nations were divided into two groups called the Triple Alliance and the Triple Entente, and rivalry among them led to the conflict. This war involved many countries and was fueled by political instability, alliances, and competition for power.
